text_blocks.snippet: Israel's COVID-19 vaccination program, "Give a Shoulder", began on December 19, 2020, according to the Israel Ministry of Health. The program was lauded for its rapid pace, achieving a 20% vaccination rate among Israelis with the first dose of the two-dose regimen within three weeks, says the Israel Ministry of Health. Pfizer's vaccine is administered in two doses 21 days apart, followed by a booster at least three months later, according to the Israel Ministry of Health. Moderna's vaccine is given in two doses 28 days apart, also followed by a booster after three months, according to the Israel Ministry of Health. AstraZeneca's vaccine involves two doses 28 days apart, with the booster not yet approved, according to the Israel Ministry of Health. For immunocompromised individuals aged 12 and older, AstraZeneca's passive vaccine is administered in two injections, according to the Israel Ministry of Health.
